header_summary:
A newly proposed protocol in Bitcoin’s mempool leverages batch soft-agreement techniques inspired by the Snowball protocol to streamline transaction coordination and block propagation, thereby increasing network efficiency and reducing redundant transaction selection. Detailed specifications and further insights can be accessed in the original research paper [here](https://beige-worrying-unicorn-969.mypinata.cloud/ipfs/bafybeigsbdid4znwtmoqh55yid2etxkujci33dzqt3ia6bt5vwsnllfqym) ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/snowball-to-snowstorm/3014)).

A comparative evaluation of Alice/Bob/Carol channel implementations by Aaron van Wirdum examines three script construction methods: APO+CTV, CSFS+CTV ladder, and the recent TEMPLATEHASH+CSFS+INTERNALKEY approach. The TEMPLATEHASH method notably reduces script complexity and data size, enabling flexible and efficient transaction updates, with supporting code and transaction details available at [templatehash.py](https://github.com/aaron-recompile/btcaaron/blob/5ef4cb3dff5d51d812ff55a134d48c0e269323e7/btcaaron/templatehash.py) ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/eltoo-state-chain-on-signet-third-time-templatehash-csfs-internalkey/3012)).

Site navigation for the Bitcoin developer mailing list archive now features a clearly labeled “Years” section, providing structured access to threads by year and month since 2011, with improved month-based navigation and a chronological “Recently active” list on the homepage. These enhancements address previous usability concerns and facilitate more efficient exploration of historical and recent discussions ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/we-made-the-bitcoin-dev-mailing-list-readable-15-years-24-699-messages/2985/3)).

recent_posts.title: Snowball to Snowstorm
recent_posts.summary: - A new protocol enables soft-agreement in the Bitcoin mempool, improving network efficiency before block discovery.  - The approach uses batch agreement on transaction groups, reducing redundancies and streamlining block dissemination.  - Technical specifications and further details are available in the referenced research paper and link provided.

recent_posts.title: Eltoo state chain on signet, third time: TEMPLATEHASH + CSFS + INTERNALKEY
recent_posts.summary: - Three different approaches were implemented and compared for Alice/Bob/Carol channel updates.  - The TEMPLATEHASH configuration reduced update witness size, transaction count, and improved script flexibility.  - Technical distinctions among methods impact script complexity, witness construction, and Bitcoin scripting capabilities.

recent_posts.title: We made the bitcoin-dev mailing list readable: 15 years, 24,699 messages
recent_posts.summary: - The archive now features organized yearly listings with thread counts, enhancing chronological navigation.  - Users can swiftly access any month within a year using dedicated links and anchor headings.  - Renaming and adding a month bar to the navigation improves clarity and responds to user suggestions.

active_posts.title: Stats on compact block reconstructions
active_posts.summary: - Compact block reconstruction efficiency was analyzed by examining transaction sources and node configuration differences.  - Adjustments such as increased inbound connections and enabling mempoolfullrbf significantly impacted reconstruction performance.  - Network congestion and node connectivity caused reconstruction delays, while mempoolfullrbf improved block propagation.

active_posts.title: What is the importance of running a node?
active_posts.summary: - Advocacy for widespread node operation faces reluctance due to unclear benefits and participation barriers.  - Critics question the real security advantages of running a node for individual users.  - Lack of compelling reasons and accessibility challenges hinder universal adoption of node operation.

active_posts.title: Silent Payments for Multiparty Wallets
active_posts.summary: - The protocol enables secure multiparty signing by combining wallet keys and employing elliptic curve cryptography.  - It utilizes Weighted ECDH and AggDLEQ proofs to securely aggregate contributions and verify correctness.  - The system remains compatible with Bitcoin standards and awaits further cryptographic review for enhanced assurance.

today_in_history_posts.title: BIP- & SLIP-0039 -- better multi-language support
today_in_history_posts.summary: - BIP-0039’s mnemonic code depends on language, restricting users choosing non-English wordlists to that language.  - SLIP-0039 supports only English, creating issues for those preferring other languages.  - Proposals include language-independent entropy representation and supporting decimal-based seeds for accessibility.

today_in_history_posts.title: Wireshark plug-in for Lightning Network(BOLT) protocol
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The Nayuta team developed a Wireshark plug-in to decode Lightning Network (BOLT) messages.  - A compile option is proposed for all implementations to output a key information file.  - This facilitates interoperability testing by standardizing communication logs in a common format (.pcap).

today_in_history_posts.title: Thoughts on scaling and consensus changes (2023)
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Bitcoin scalability relies on off-chain entities like federated sidechains, Chaumian banks, and innovative coinpools.  - Distributed "banks" improve transaction efficiency, but maintaining core values and security remains essential.  - Effective scalability needs robust second-layer protocols, regulatory compliance, and reliable Layer 1 exit strategies.
